title: Reproducing the QAIDR manuscript results
text: T&C, MRRE, LCMC families follow Lee Verleysen (2009). MRRE uses printed rank weights, B_LC bounded B_NX = U_X - U_N. Positive behavior values mean intrusion dominance. Ranks exclude self-distances. Primary cells tie-free; unavoidable structural ties use 50 seeded uniform resolutions, flagged, report maximum resolution spread. Permutations apply one uniform label bijection endpoints embedded ranks. P-values use (c + 1)/(m + 1) m = 999. Single-step Westfall–Young min-P adjustment controls multiplicity within index family across metrics method fixed K. simulation study uses 100 independently seeded datasets per scenario reports standard deviations Monte Carlo standard errors. Calibration evaluated prespecified subset replications. Center-Euclidean baselines measure interval widths add beyond midpoints.

title: Introduction to QAIDR
text: QAIDR (Quality Assessment Interval-based Dimensionality Reduction) provides tools evaluating interval DR methods using co-ranking matrices. supports: 4 interval distance metrics: Interval Euclidean, Hausdorff, Ichino-Yaguchi, L2-Wasserstein 3 quality/behavior index families: T&C, MRRE, LCMC (6 indices total) 6 DR methods: C-PCA, V-PCA, MR-PCA, SPCA, IMDS, Int-UMAP Statistical tests: permutation inference family-wise adjustment Baselines: center-assessment isolate information widths

title: Introduction to QAIDR
text: Interval-valued data consists observations variable interval [,b][, b], represented internally center (+b)/2(+b)/2 radius (b−)/2(b-)/2. can also create interval data common formats:
code: library(QAIDR)  # From centers and radii matrices C <- matrix(rnorm(40), 10, 4) R <- matrix(runif(40, 0.1, 0.5), 10, 4) x <- interval_data(C, R, labels = rep(c("A", "B"), each = 5)) print(x) #> interval_data: 10 observations, 4 variables #> Labels: A, B # From a min-max data frame df <- data.frame(   A.min = c(1, 3, 5), A.max = c(2, 5, 8),   B.min = c(10, 20, 30), B.max = c(12, 25, 35),   class = c("x", "y", "x") ) x2 <- interval_data_from_mm(df, int_min_at = c(1, 3), y_at = 5) print(x2) #> interval_data: 3 observations, 2 variables #> Labels: x, y  # From a 3D array (n x p x 2) arr <- array(c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 2, 4, 5, 6, 8, 9), dim = c(3, 2, 2)) x3 <- interval_data_from_array(arr)

title: Introduction to QAIDR

title: Introduction to QAIDR
text: typical QAIDR workflow : Load create interval_data Standardize standardize() Run DR methods run_idr() Assess quality assess_quality() Visualize plot_projections() plot_k_profiles() See “Real Data Analysis” “Simulation Study” vignettes compact tutorials. complete seeded manuscript pipeline frozen outputs documented README_REPRODUCIBILITY.md GitHub repository.
code: # Complete example (requires dataSDA, symbolicDA, RSDA, umap, and dplyr) data("cars.int", package = "dataSDA") cars <- interval_data_from_dataSDA(cars.int) x <- standardize(cars)  proj <- run_idr(x) result <- assess_quality(x, proj, K = 5, perm_test = TRUE, n_perm = 999,                          baseline = TRUE) print(result)  plot_projections(proj, labels = cars$labels)  profiles <- k_profiles(x, proj, K_max = 20) plot_k_profiles(profiles, metric = "Wasserstein")

title: Real-Data Examples with QAIDR
text: cars.int contains 27 car models, four interval-valued variables (Price, Engine Capacity, Top Speed, Acceleration), class variable. conversion keeps model names stored data’s concept attribute uses singleton symbolic sets class labels. Run available DR methods inspect projected rectangles: Assess every method–dissimilarity pair K = 5. center-row essential comparison: shows whether interval widths add assessment information beyond midpoints alone. default 999 permutations permit finite-sample p-values 0.05, pvalues_adj contains within-family Westfall–Young min-P adjustment. Quality behavior can also inspected across neighborhood sizes:
code: library(QAIDR) data("cars.int", package = "dataSDA")  cars <- interval_data_from_dataSDA(cars.int) print(cars) summary(cars) x_cars <- standardize(cars) set.seed(20260718) proj_cars <- run_idr(x_cars) plot_projections(proj_cars, labels = cars$labels,                  obs_labels = rownames(cars$centers)) cars_assessment <- assess_quality(   x_cars, proj_cars, K = 5,   perm_test = TRUE, n_perm = 999,   seed = 20260719, baseline = TRUE ) print(cars_assessment) cars_assessment$pvalues_adj cars_profiles <- k_profiles(x_cars, proj_cars, K_max = 20, baseline = TRUE) plot_k_profiles(cars_profiles, metric = "Wasserstein")

title: Real-Data Examples with QAIDR

title: Real-Data Examples with QAIDR
text: Higher quality values indicate better neighborhood preservation. Behavior values near zero indicate balance; positive values consistently indicate intrusion-dominated embedding, negative values indicate extrusion-dominated embedding. Interpret isolated values together K-profiles, tie diagnostics, center-baseline, adjusted permutation results.

title: Assess quality of interval DR projections — assess_quality
text: Computes adjudicated quality behavior indices combination DR method interval dissimilarity, optionally permutation inference. P-values use finite-sample Monte Carlo estimator (c + 1) / (m + 1) throughout. perm_test = TRUE, family-wise adjusted p-values additionally computed single-step Westfall-Young min-P resampling using shared joint permutation draws; multiplicity family , per DR method index family (T&C, MRRE, LCMC) fixed K, set {quality, behavior} tests across requested metrics. Quality tests one-sided (upper); behavior tests two-sided.

what: Rank matrix with self-exclusion and tie detection — rank_matrix
title: Rank matrix with self-exclusion and tie detection — rank_matrix
text: Computes, observation, ranks observations distance, excluding self-distance ranking. Ranks take values 1, ..., N-1. -diagonal ties detected within scale-aware tolerance; primary (default) policy ties = "error" tie aborts error, ordinary tie-free cells computed strict rank systems assumed co-ranking theory. opt-ties = "random" resolves tolerance-connected tie block uniform random ordering whole block (seed session RNG reproducibility); used explicitly labelled tie audits daggered structural-tie cells, results summarized seeded repeated resolutions, never used silently ranks tie-free. Randomization covers every detected block, including near-ties whose members exactly equal (base R's random tie method alone randomize exact equals).

title: Rank matrix with self-exclusion and tie detection — rank_matrix
code: rank_matrix(D, ties = c("error", "random"), tol = 1e-12)

title: Rank matrix with self-exclusion and tie detection — rank_matrix
text: D Numeric symmetric distance/dissimilarity matrix (n x n), non-negative, zero diagonal. ties Character, one "error" (primary) "random" (documented fallback). tol Numeric relative tolerance used tie detection (default 1e-12): two consecutive sorted distances tie gap tol times larger two. default catches structural ties (duplicate objects, coincident interval geometry) ignoring floating-point near-misses genuinely distinct distances.

title: Rank matrix with self-exclusion and tie detection — rank_matrix
text: Integer matrix (n x n) ranks 0 diagonal row's -diagonal entries permutation 1:(n-1). Attribute "n_ties" total number adjacent tolerance links sorted -diagonal rows; tolerance-connected block size b contributes b - 1.

title: Rank matrix with self-exclusion and tie detection — rank_matrix
code: D <- as.matrix(dist(matrix(rnorm(30), 10, 3))) R <- rank_matrix(D)

title: QAIDR 0.2.0 (2026-07-18)
text: Correctness release implementing adjudicated index specification Lee Verleysen (2009), Neurocomputing 72:1431–1443. Results produced QAIDR 0.1.0 MRRE LCMC-behavior families comparable regenerated.

title: QAIDR 0.2.0 (2026-07-18)
text: rank_matrix(ties = "random") now uniformly randomizes every tolerance-detected tie block whole (transitive adjacent near-tie chains included). Previously detected blocks passed base R’s rank(..., ties.method = "random"), randomizes exactly equal values, detected near-ties exactly equal never randomized. Tie-free ranks bit--bit unchanged consume RNG; published daggered cells (caused exact structural duplicates) unaffected, confirmed tie-impact audit. .check_dist() now accepts n = 3 observations, matching null calibration theorem’s domain (n >= 3, K <= n - 2). idist_euclidean() validates lambda directly (one finite numeric scalar [0, 1]) instead relying idist() dispatcher. idist_hausdorff() documentation now states explicitly computes coordinatewise product-Hausdorff dissimilarity (L2 aggregation per-coordinate interval Hausdorff distances), set-Hausdorff metric hyperrectangles. metric key "Hausdorff" unchanged. rank_matrix() documentation now explains n_ties attribute counts adjacent tolerance links (block size b contributes b - 1) describes seeded structural-tie protocol used manuscript.

title: QAIDR 0.2.0 (2026-07-18)
text: coranking_indices() MRRE now follows printed Lee–Verleysen Eqs. (10)–(12): W_n sums pairs low-space rank l <= K weight |k-l|/l; W_v sums pairs high-space rank k <= K weight |k-l|/k. 0.1.0 implementation omitted upper-left block sums; Q_RE B_RE values change. B_LC now Lee–Verleysen’s behavior index B_NX (Eqs. 22–23): B_LC = U_X - U_N computed strict triangles K--K upper-left block. 0.1.0 upper region unbounded therefore nonzero null mean. Positive values indicate intrusion-dominated embeddings. Ranks computed excluding self-distance (rank_matrix()). 0.1.0 rank--diagonal--subtract approach silently drop pairs duplicate observations violate sum(Q) = n(n-1). Index values longer clamped nominal ranges; --range values raise diagnostic warning instead.

title: QAIDR 0.2.0 (2026-07-18)
text: Primary analyses error detected -diagonal distance ties (ties = "error"). documented, seeded fallback (ties = "random") resolves tolerance-detected tie blocks uniformly random. perm_test() assess_quality() share one permutation engine use finite-sample estimator p = (c + 1)/(m + 1); default n_perm = 999. Single-step Westfall–Young min-P family-wise adjusted p-values (pvalues_adj) provided within index family (T&C, MRRE, LCMC) fixed K, across metrics, per DR method, reusing joint permutation draws. center-Euclidean baseline row (baseline = TRUE) available assess_quality() k_profiles(). idist() exposes lambda (Interval Euclidean optimism index) nu (Ichino–Yaguchi span weight); idist_ichino_yaguchi() renames gamma nu (deprecated alias retained). k_profiles() computes co-ranking matrix per method-metric pair evaluates K . Int-UMAP wrapper passes configuration object RSDA::sym.umap() records effective configuration. New exported building blocks: rank_matrix(), coranking_matrix(), indices_from_coranking(), perm_null_indices(). New interval_data_from_dataSDA() converter loads Cars Face examples suggested CRAN package dataSDA; QAIDR longer redistributes copies datasets. Package metadata now credits Paulo Canas Rodrigues Han-Ming Wu authors.
